_note: The editor's decisions on the 'For you' lines after the second readers' notes (702, 718). Each change makes a line say less than its confirmed sources, never more; emergency guidance stays the senior author's to change.

line.line: It is time to call an ambulance for trouble breathing, a fit, or panic that will not calm down.
line.why: Second reader 702: the clause 'Fear alone does not always need an ambulance' rests on one publisher, and another of the line's own sources lists intense fear of dying among its signs for calling. The clause is taken out; the three signs stay as checked.

line.line: If you are not being sick, drink some water in small sips.
line.why: Second reader 718's suggested wording: the NHS anchor gives water only to someone who is conscious, able to swallow and not vomiting.

only.why: Readers 701 and 718: the lines were written from pages about cannabis; the sources say synthetic cannabinoids can cause death or serious harm and that the 'not life-threatening' sentence holds for cannabis alone. The block is shown on the cannabis page only; the synthetic cannabinoids page keeps its lines for helping a friend and for calling an ambulance.
